goal: Compare the methods reported in the three uploaded papers with experiment.xlsx results. Find the best configuration under 3M parameters, generate a chart, and assess whether our results support the reported design advantages. Use only uploaded data and documents; these are synthetic fixtures.
answer:
## What the papers report

| Paper | Method | Design | Params | Reported mIoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| paper_1.pdf | A | Convolutional segmentation | 2.5M | 73.27 |
| paper_2.pdf | B | Attention segmentation | 3.2M | 76.0 |
| paper_3.pdf | C | Compact convolution baseline | 2.0M | 70.0 |

[paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]

All three PDFs state that the values are synthetic test values, not published research claims. They also state that the methods use the same fixture benchmark and evaluation protocol, that the claims are descriptive quality/cost tradeoff claims only, with no causal or ablation claim, and that there are three fixture configurations with no uncertainty estimates. [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]

## What experiment.xlsx contains

`experiment.xlsx` has one sheet (`Sheet1`) with 3 rows and 3 columns: `model` (text), `params_m` (float), and `miou` (float), with no missing values. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]

| model | params_m | miou |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2.5 | 73.27 |
| B | 3.2 | 76.0 |
| C | 2.0 | 70.0 |

These values match the paper-reported figures. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7] [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]

## Best configuration under 3M parameters

Applying the `params_m < 3.0` filter leaves two candidates:

- **A — 2.5M params, mIoU 73.27**
- **C — 2.0M params, mIoU 70.00**

**Best under 3M: Model A** at 2.5M parameters and 73.27 mIoU. B is excluded because it is at 3.2M. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]

## Artifacts

The analysis execution produced artifact files named `comparison.png` and `summary.json`. The computed output says a summary was written to `summary.json`. The supplied evidence does not describe the chart type or annotations, so I won’t characterize the plot beyond the artifact filenames. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]

## Does the supplied data support the reported design advantages?

**Only in the narrow, descriptive sense that the papers themselves claim.**

- **A vs C:** the fixture data show A improving mIoU by 3.27 points over C for 0.5M more parameters, matching the reported tradeoff. [paper_3.pdf, p.1] [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]
- **B vs A:** B improves mIoU by 2.73 points over A for 0.7M more parameters, again matching the reported tradeoff. [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1] [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]

The experiment file restates the same three values, and the ordering is **B > A > C** for mIoU, with parameter counts also ordered **B > A > C**. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7]

**Important limits on that conclusion:**

1. The experiment file contains the same three values as the papers — it is a restatement, not independent corroboration. The supplied evidence does not provide a separate held-out measurement. [Analysis 242dcec8-5370-410d-b8cc-710c534fe4f7] [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]
2. Only three configurations are reported, with no uncertainty estimates in the fixture notes, so I would not treat the numeric gaps as statistically established based on the supplied evidence. [paper_3.pdf, p.1]
3. The papers disclaim causal or ablation claims; with one configuration per method, the observed gains cannot be attributed to the architectural choices (convolution vs attention vs compact baseline). Any “attention beats convolution” reading is unsupported by this data. [paper_1.pdf, p.1] [paper_2.pdf, p.1] [paper_3.pdf, p.1]
4. The materials are explicitly synthetic fixtures, so results should not be extrapolated to real benchmarks. [paper_3.pdf, p.1]

**Bottom line:** if the goal is a sub-3M deployment budget, Model A (2.5M params, 73.27 mIoU) is the best-supported pick from the uploaded data. The results are consistent with the papers’ descriptive cost/quality tradeoff claims, but they do not establish that the design choices caused the gains.
